tidbit: Did you know… this hour's top stories come from five different outlets.
transcript:
Hourly brief, Founders' Preview. Here is what is moving in superintelligence (SI), the next generation of artificial intelligence (AI).
Anthropic's Agent4Sci evaluates artificial intelligence agents on 20 scientific benchmarks. Reported by 36Kr: Claude Opus shows 10.4% average improvement, though agents still cannot conduct genuine real-world scientific research.
Chinese artificial intelligence firms used pirated Korean books to train models. Reported by Korea JoongAng Daily: DeepSeek has reproduced text from Han Kang, implicating Huawei and DeepSeek in the unauthorized use.
Sweden blocks ChatGPT and Claude from government computers. Confirmed by Digit: the country mandates Microsoft Copilot for government staff instead.
Artificial intelligence agents exhibit playful behavior in simulations that improves their task performance. Reported by PCMag Middle East: agents like to play without work obligations.
Australia's first major artificial intelligence data center proposal faces local opposition. Reported by CNN: Anthropic's project encounters pushback from the rural town over water and energy use.
Free every hour.
